clue.text: A great number will turn awkward and shout

indicators.note: to turn awkward is to go wrong or out of order, so the two words that follow get rearranged

explanation.surface: Many people will become difficult and start yelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn awkward' rearranges the eight letters of AND SHOUT; 'will' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is a large round figure, the kind of count meant by a great many.

clue.text: Set about forming an outfit

explanation.surface: Someone starts putting together a set of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To set about a job is to take it on with vigour; an angler's or sailor's gear and equipment is also called by this word.

clue.text: In fashion for all young people, so it's said

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning parts of three of them

explanation.surface: A trend that every teenager follows, or so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'for' through 'all' to the first letter of 'young'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by mouth is spoken rather than written, which is what 'so it's said' describes.

clue.text: Only sherry will be offered in such a ship

definitions.text: Only sherry will be offered in such a ship

parts.words: Only sherry will be offered in such a ship
parts.note: reads like a vessel with a strange drinks policy, but the same name covers a tall glass for sherry and a fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A cruise vessel that serves nothing but fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a large sherry glass carries the same name as a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Joshua's father's sisters

explanation.surface: The Biblical leader's dad had female siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Joshua is called 'the son of Nun', so his father's name with an apostrophe-s gives the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical Joshua's father was named Nun, and women in religious orders are called sisters.

clue.text: Free with money

explanation.surface: Something given away along with cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To free a captive by paying is to redeem them, and the payment demanded by kidnappers is the same word.

clue.text: A group of managers who have got on?

parts.note: a company's governing body of directors is its board

explanation.surface: Asks about a committee of executives who have made a success of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got on' looks like 'prospered', but here it means boarded a vehicle or ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers who have got on a train or ship are now on board it.

clue.text: His stock is extremely small — should grow though

definitions.text: His stock is extremely small — should grow though

parts.words: His stock is extremely small — should grow though
parts.note: sounds like a trader with a tiny inventory hoping for expansion, but the stock in question is tiny things that sprout into plants

explanation.surface: A trader whose inventory is tiny hopes the business will expand.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in seeds sells tiny goods that grow into plants once sown.

clue.text: Trade in film that's improperly distributed

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other, the trade term going within the film term

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on a window
to trade is to deal

explanation.surface: Commerce in cinema that has been unfairly shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests cinema; it is a fine haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing cards wrongly is giving them out incorrectly, the sense of handing things round improperly.

clue.text: Realising about fifty may be ill-matched

indicators.note: the realising word goes around the Roman numeral, surrounding it

parts.note: realising assets is cashing them in
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Becoming aware of being around fifty might make one feel out of step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Realising' looks like understanding but means converting to money.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours that clash jar with each other, so they are badly paired.

clue.text: They have a certain partiality for left-overs!

parts.note: taken as written: the rest of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: People who are fond of eating up yesterday's scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'left-overs' splits in two: L for left plus OVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: People in love are fond of someone, a partiality for one particular person.

clue.text: Going after an old palace

parts.note: something that goes after comes later in time

explanation.surface: Someone is hunting for an ancient royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going after' suggests pursuit but means following on in time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lateran in Rome was the principal residence of the popes for centuries.

clue.text: See a couple of trainees work, being idle

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate, so two of them are LL
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Watch a pair of apprentices doing a job while lazing about.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for a learner (British learner drivers display an L-plate).
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to lounge or loaf about lazily, so it means to idle.

clue.text: A ball-game — note scores made

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: made here means made into something new, so the letters of scores are refashioned

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture where points are noted as they are scored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges SCORES into CROSSE, placed after LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with a ball and netted sticks.

clue.text: Oils in a compound bond

indicators.note: as a verb, to compound is to mix together, so these letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: Oils mixed in a chemical compound form a link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' and 'bond' both sound like chemistry; one is the anagram signal, the other the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a close connection or tie between people or groups.

clue.text: Railed against but found release in retirement

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the word for release is read backwards

parts.note: to deliver someone is to release or set them free

explanation.surface: Someone who complained bitterly found freedom once they stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reads DELIVER backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail against something is to denounce it abusively, which is what it means to have abused it verbally.

clue.text: Chance collapse

explanation.surface: An accidental breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance is to happen, as in 'if it should befall'; to collapse is to tumble down.

clue.text: Beasts responsible for the present transport system

definitions.text: Beasts responsible for the present transport system

parts.words: Beasts responsible for the present transport system
parts.note: reads as if about today's public transport, but 'present' means a gift, as carried by Santa's sleigh team

explanation.surface: Animals blamed for the state of today's transport network.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christmas lore, Father Christmas's sleigh of gifts is pulled by antlered deer.

clue.text: Study progress, but not in favour of meeting

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn

indicators.note: the following words are removed from progress

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Examine headway, but disapprove of a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes PRO from PROGRESS, leaving GRESS after CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A congress is a formal assembly or conference of delegates.

clue.text: Leaving out nothing on purpose

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
a mission is a vocation or purpose

explanation.surface: Excluding nothing deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on purpose' looks like a phrase meaning deliberately; 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is the act of excluding something, a gerund in the same sense.

clue.text: Egghead not backing the public school

parts.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter, E

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word not is read from right to left

explanation.surface: An intellectual who does not support the well-known private school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives E, the head of 'egg'. ETON is a famous English boarding school; in Britain 'public school' means a fee-paying one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the best-known of the English fee-paying schools.

clue.text: Placates underworld members

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the name for the underworld itself
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Calms down gangland gang members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests gangsters; it is the classical land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to win them over and soothe hostility.

clue.text: Toil hard, so take rest possibly about four

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the Roman numeral
possibly says the letters of rest may be arranged another way

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Work hard, so perhaps take a break around four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns REST into STRE, and 'about' puts it around IV.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make a great effort, working hard at something.

clue.text: Sending up a chap with a soft hat

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

indicators.note: in a down clue sending up means reading upwards, so a chap is turned around

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Mocking a fellow who is wearing a floppy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sending up' looks like mockery but reverses A MAN to NAMA, placed after P and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight straw sun hat.

clue.text: A woman's time shows on this

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: A woman's age shows on her face.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereon is a formal word meaning upon this point or thing.

clue.text: "Antigone" translation causing disagreement

indicators.note: translating changes a text's form, so the title's letters are rendered into a new order

explanation.surface: A version of Sophocles' tragedy causes an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Antigone is a Greek tragedy by Sophocles.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is denial or contradiction, a refusal to agree.

clue.text: Property of oriental, say

parts.note: E stands for east, and oriental means eastern
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: Land belonging to someone from the East, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a landed holding, a large piece of real property.

clue.text: Inconsistent statement in pope's document

explanation.surface: A contradiction found in a papal decree.
explanation.walkthrough: An Irish bull is a self-contradictory statement; a papal bull is an edict from the pope.
explanation.definitionFit: A ludicrously self-contradictory remark is called a bull, and an official papal edict sealed with a bulla has the same name.

clue.text: This is truly nauseating stuff!

parts.note: reads like a complaint about something disgusting, but literally describes a substance meant to make you sick

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that something is utterly revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a medicine given to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Contemplate putting alcoholic drink in tea perhaps

parts.note: rum is a spirit
taken as written

indicators.note: perhaps signals that tea may appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Consider lacing a cuppa with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns TEA into ATE, after RUM and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to ponder or think deeply about something.

clue.text: Bacon could be comparatively audacious

explanation.surface: Francis Bacon might have been a bolder figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of bacon is a rasher, and someone more reckless than another is the comparative of rash.

clue.text: A fruit worker given spartan accommodation

indicators.note: the austere word accommodates the worker, holding it inside

parts.note: spartan means plain and austere
a worker is an ant, the sterile female of the colony

explanation.surface: An employee is given basic, no-frills lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: A worker in crosswords is usually an ant (or bee).
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a starchy banana-like fruit, usually cooked before eating.
